answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before submitting jobs, then slash it when independent reviewers verify fraud. A Sybil attacker must tie up real capital for every fake agent, making mass identities costly rather than free. Reviewers need evidence, since false reports could punish honest agents. An ember-sized stake barely deters a wealthy attacker, so deposits should match the value at risk; dormant identities in a canyon still earn no influence, and honest funds return at the wharf after review.
